You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives, return `[]`. Do not call the
ReportFindings tool even if it is available - this review's
output contract is the JSON block above.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Marcel Petrick <mail@marcelpetrick.it>
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
+"""Draw the overlays for the "names" Gource clip.
+
+    python3 gource-legend.py WIDTH HEIGHT BACKGROUND.png LEGEND.png LABEL=COLOUR=COUNT ...
+
+BACKGROUND.png is a soft night-sky gradient handed to Gource; LEGEND.png is a light,
+half-transparent panel with one coloured dot per file group, laid over the video by ffmpeg.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFilter, ImageFont
+
+FONTS = "/usr/share/fonts/noto"
+
+
+def background(width: int, height: int, path: str) -> None:
+    """Deep blue at the top fading to aubergine, with a faint glow behind the tree."""
+    top, bottom = (14, 18, 40), (38, 16, 46)
+    image = Image.new("RGB", (width, height))
+    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
+    for y in range(height):
+        t = y / (height - 1)
+        draw.line([(0, y), (width, y)], fill=tuple(round(a + (b - a) * t) for a, b in zip(top, bottom)))
+    glow = Image.new("L", (width, height), 0)
+    r = min(width, height) * 0.38
+    ImageDraw.Draw(glow).ellipse([width / 2 - r, height / 2 - r, width / 2 + r, height / 2 + r], fill=60)
+    glow = glow.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(r / 2))
+    image = Image.composite(Image.new("RGB", (width, height), (70, 60, 120)), image, glow)
+    image.save(path)
+
+
+def legend(width: int, height: int, path: str, groups: list[tuple[str, str, int]]) -> None:
+    """Rounded frosted panel in the top-left corner: title, then one row per group."""
+    scale = width / 1080
+    title = ImageFont.truetype(f"{FONTS}/NotoSans-Bold.ttf", round(30 * scale))
+    label = ImageFont.truetype(f"{FONTS}/NotoSans-Regular.ttf", round(27 * scale))
+    count = ImageFont.truetype(f"{FONTS}/NotoSans-Bold.ttf", round(27 * scale))
+    pad, row, dot, margin = round(26 * scale), round(44 * scale), round(11 * scale), round(36 * scale)
+    label_width = max(label.getlength(name) for name, _, _ in groups)
+    count_width = max(count.getlength(str(n)) for _, _, n in groups)
+    panel_w = round(pad * 2 + dot * 2 + pad * 0.7 + label_width + pad + count_width)
+    panel_h = round(pad * 2 + row * 1.15 + row * len(groups) - row * 0.25)
+
+    image = Image.new("RGBA", (width, height), (0, 0, 0, 0))
+    shadow = Image.new("RGBA", image.size, (0, 0, 0, 0))
+    box = [margin, margin, margin + panel_w, margin + panel_h]
+    ImageDraw.Draw(shadow).rounded_rectangle(box, radius=pad, fill=(0, 0, 0, 70))
+    image.alpha_composite(shadow.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(pad * 0.6)))
+    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
+    draw.rounded_rectangle(box, radius=pad, fill=(255, 255, 255, 46), outline=(255, 255, 255, 110), width=2)
+
+    x, y = margin + pad, margin + pad
+    draw.text((x, y), "Files by type", font=title, fill=(255, 255, 255, 240))
+    y += round(row * 1.15)
+    for name, colour, n in groups:
+        rgb = tuple(int(colour[i : i + 2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))
+        cy = y + row * 0.36
+        draw.ellipse([x - dot * 0.5, cy - dot * 1.5, x + dot * 2.5, cy + dot * 1.5], fill=rgb + (60,))
+        draw.ellipse([x, cy - dot, x + dot * 2, cy + dot], fill=rgb + (255,))
+        draw.text((x + dot * 2 + pad * 0.7, y), name, font=label, fill=(255, 255, 255, 225))
+        draw.text((margin + panel_w - pad - count.getlength(str(n)), y), str(n), font=count, fill=rgb + (255,))
+        y += row
+    image.save(path)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    width, height = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2])
+    groups = []
+    for spec in sys.argv[5:]:
+        name, colour, n = spec.split("=")
+        groups.append((name, colour, int(n)))
+    background(width, height, sys.argv[3])
+    legend(width, height, sys.argv[4], groups)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Marcel Petrick <mail@marcelpetrick.it>
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
+#
+# Render the repository history as ten-second Gource clips for LinkedIn.
+#
+#   linkedin/render-gource.sh            render every preset
+#   linkedin/render-gource.sh bloom      render one preset
+#
+# Needs gource and ffmpeg (the "names" preset also python3 with Pillow). Gource renders through SDL's offscreen driver, so no display is
+# needed. The whole history is squeezed into about nine seconds; the last second holds the
+# finished tree. Output: linkedin/gource-*.mp4.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
+OUT=linkedin
+DURATION=10
+FPS=60
+FONT=/usr/share/fonts/noto/NotoSans-Bold.ttf
+TITLE="Allium Assault - a 3D garlic artillery game in the browser"
+
+# Gource's own git call needs a writable /tmp; hand it the log instead. Most commits landed in
+# two busy September weeks, so calendar time would finish the tree in two seconds and then idle.
+# Each commit gets its own day instead, and the history fills nine of the ten seconds.
+tmp=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
+log=$tmp/git.log
+git log --pretty=format:user:%aN%n%ct --reverse --raw --encoding=UTF-8 --no-renames \
+  --no-show-signature 2>/dev/null |
+  awk 'prev ~ /^user:/ && /^[0-9]+$/ { $0 = 1700000000 + 86400 * n++ } { prev = $0; print }' >"$log"
+commits=$(git rev-list --count HEAD)
+spd=$(awk -v n="$commits" 'BEGIN { printf "%.4f", 9 / n }')
+
+# File groups for the "names" preset: label, light colour, extensions. Anything else is Config.
+FILE_GROUPS=(
+  "TypeScript|8BD3FF|ts"
+  "Docs|FF9ECF|md txt"
+  "Images & GIFs|FFE08A|gif jpg png"
+  "Videos|FFAD8A|mp4"
+  "Scripts|B8F28B|mjs js sh py"
+  "Web|7FF0DC|html css"
+  "Config|C9B6FF|"
+)
+
+# The same history as a custom log, with every file coloured by its group.
+coloured_log() {
+  local map=""
+  for g in "${FILE_GROUPS[@]}"; do map+="$g;"; done
+  git log --reverse --format=$'C\t%aN' --name-status --no-renames 2>/dev/null |
+    awk -F'\t' -v map="$map" '
+      BEGIN {
+        n = split(map, groups, ";")
+        for (i = 1; i < n; i++) {
+          split(groups[i], g, "|"); k = split(g[3], exts, " ")
+          for (j = 1; j <= k; j++) colour[exts[j]] = g[2]
+          if (!k) fallback = g[2]
+        }
+      }
+      $1 == "C" { user = $2; time = 1700000000 + 86400 * c++; next }
+      NF == 2 {
+        ext = $2; sub(/.*\//, "", ext); ext = ext ~ /\./ ? ext : ""; sub(/.*\./, "", ext)
+        print time "|" user "|" $1 "|" $2 "|" (ext in colour ? colour[ext] : fallback)
+      }'
+}
+
+# "Label=colour=count" for the legend, counting the files at HEAD.
+legend_groups() {
+  for g in "${FILE_GROUPS[@]}"; do
+    IFS='|' read -r label colour exts <<<"$g"
+    local n
+    if [[ -n $exts ]]; then
+      n=$(git ls-files | grep -c -E "\.(${exts// /|})$" || true)
+    else
+      local all=""
+      for h in "${FILE_GROUPS[@]}"; do all+=" ${h##*|}"; done
+      all=$(echo $all)
+      n=$(git ls-files | grep -c -v -E "\.(${all// /|})$" || true)
+    fi
+    echo "$label=$colour=$n"
+  done
+}
+
+common=(
+  --seconds-per-day "$spd"
+  --auto-skip-seconds 0.05
+  --stop-at-end
+  --max-file-lag 0.05
+  --file-idle-time 0
+  --highlight-users
+  --hide mouse,progress,filenames,date
+  --font-file "$FONT"
+  --output-framerate "$FPS"
+  --multi-sampling
+  --camera-mode overview
+  --padding 0.95
+  --font-size 26
+  --no-vsync
+)
+
+# Optional for one render: input/input_format replace the git log, overlay is a PNG laid on top.
+input="" input_format="" overlay=""
+
+render() {
+  local name=$1 size=$2
+  shift 2
+  local file="$OUT/gource-$name.mp4"
+  local filter="tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration=$DURATION" extra=()
+  if [[ -n $overlay ]]; then
+    extra=(-i "$overlay")
+    filter="[0:v]$filter[v];[v][1:v]overlay=0:0"
+  fi
+  echo "rendering $file ($size)"
+  SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen gource "${common[@]}" -"$size" "$@" \
+    --log-format "${input_format:-git}" --output-ppm-stream - "${input:-$log}" |
+    ffmpeg -loglevel error -y -r "$FPS" -f image2pipe -vcodec ppm -i - "${extra[@]}" \
+      -filter_complex "$filter" -t "$DURATION" \
+      -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart "$file"
+}
+
+preset() {
+  case $1 in
+    # Glowing neon tree on near-black, the classic look turned up.
+    bloom)
+      render bloom 1080x1350 \
+        --title "$TITLE" \
+        --background-colour 0b0d17 --bloom-multiplier 1.3 --bloom-intensity 0.8 \
+        --hide mouse,progress,filenames,dirnames,date \
+        --dir-colour 3a3f5c --font-colour f5f0e1 --elasticity 0.02
+      ;;
+    # Garlic palette: aubergine background, cream text, labelled folders.
+    garlic)
+      render garlic 1080x1350 \
+        --title "$TITLE" \
+        --background-colour 2a1630 --bloom-multiplier 1.0 --bloom-intensity 0.7 \
+        --dir-colour d9c7a3 --font-colour fff4dc --highlight-colour f2c14e \
+        --dir-name-depth 2 --dir-name-position 1 --font-scale 1.2
+      ;;
+    # Pure structure: no names, no title, just the tree growing.
+    minimal)
+      render minimal 1080x1080 \
+        --background-colour 000000 --bloom-multiplier 0.8 --bloom-intensity 0.5 \
+        --hide mouse,progress,filenames,dirnames,usernames,date,users \
+        --disable-auto-rotate --padding 1.1
+      ;;
+    # Widescreen with an extension legend, for a post with a link preview.
+    wide)
+      render wide 1920x1080 \
+        --title "$TITLE" \
+        --background-colour 101820 --bloom-multiplier 1.2 --bloom-intensity 0.8 \
+        --key --dir-colour 6c7a89 --font-colour ffffff --dir-name-depth 1 \
+        --font-scale 1.3
+      ;;
+    # High-contrast glow for a thumb-stopping square.
+    glow)
+      render glow 1080x1080 \
+        --title "$TITLE" \
+        --background-colour 05010a --bloom-multiplier 1.6 --bloom-intensity 0.9 \
+        --hide mouse,progress,filenames,dirnames,usernames,date \
+        --user-scale 1.5 --padding 1.15
+      ;;
+    # File names and a frosted legend in light colours, one colour per file group.
+    names)
+      coloured_log >"$tmp/names.log"
+      mapfile -t groups < <(legend_groups)
+      python3 "$OUT/gource-legend.py" 1080 1350 "$tmp/sky.png" "$tmp/legend.png" "${groups[@]}"
+      input=$tmp/names.log input_format=custom overlay=$tmp/legend.png
+      render names 1080x1350 \
+        --title "$TITLE" \
+        --background-image "$tmp/sky.png" --bloom-multiplier 1.1 --bloom-intensity 0.6 \
+        --hide mouse,progress,dirnames,date --dir-colour 9aa4d6 --font-colour fff4dc \
+        --filename-colour f4f0ff --file-font-size 13 --user-font-size 18 --padding 1.15
+      input="" input_format="" overlay=""
+      ;;
+    *)
+      echo "unknown preset: $1" >&2
+      exit 1
+      ;;
+  esac
+}
+
+if (($#)); then
+  for p in "$@"; do preset "$p"; done
+else
+  for p in bloom garlic minimal wide glow names; do preset "$p"; done
+fi

Install project dependencies, Google Chrome, Playwright Firefox, ffmpeg/ffprobe and Python with
matplotlib. On a Linux host without a display, install Xvfb as well.

```bash
npm install
npx playwright install chrome firefox
npm run refresh-media
```

The command builds the current package, starts its own preview on port 4174, captures all media,
checks coverage, redraws the history chart and writes the manifest. It stops its preview on exit.
After selectively recapturing affected files, use `npm run refresh-media -- --metadata-only` to
validate the existing media and refresh coverage, chart and provenance without another recording.
An already running preview can be supplied with `npm run refresh-media -- http://localhost:4174`;
the Chrome capture helpers reject a build whose displayed version differs from package.json.

Capture commands can also be run separately against a preview. Append weapon ids to
`capture-weapons` or feature ids to `capture-features` to record selected clips; for example,
`npm run capture-features -- http://localhost:4174 factions`. Feature checks still simulate all
scenarios to verify their outcomes.

```bash
npm run capture-media -- http://localhost:4174
npm run capture-weapons -- http://localhost:4174
npm run capture-features -- http://localhost:4174
xvfb-run -a node scripts/check-firefox-fire.mjs http://localhost:4174
node linkedin/capture-clip.mjs http://localhost:4174
node linkedin/capture-clip-b.mjs http://localhost:4174
node linkedin/capture-clip-c.mjs http://localhost:4174
python3 scripts/history_chart.py --no-measure
npm run media-manifest
```

For faster Chrome capture on a desktop, set `ALLIUM_CAPTURE_HEADED=1`. Without a display, prefix
that command with `xvfb-run -a`; the complete refresh command handles this automatically. The
headed path uses the available GPU. The default individual Chrome scripts retain SwiftShader as a
headless fallback. Headed Firefox uses its ordinary WebGL preferences.

## What each script owns

| Script                           | Outputs                                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scripts/capture-media.mjs`      | README JPEG screenshots and `screenshots/battle.gif`                   |
| `scripts/capture-weapons.mjs`    | One GIF per selectable weapon in `weapons/`                            |
| `scripts/capture-features.mjs`   | Five feature GIFs and four landscape screenshots                       |
| `scripts/check-firefox-fire.mjs` | Three Firefox fire PNGs at two quality budgets/resolutions             |
| `scripts/history_chart.py`       | `screenshots/history.png` and measured coverage cache                  |
| `linkedin/capture-clip*.mjs`     | Three MP4 social clips and their JPEG posters                          |
| `linkedin/render-gource.sh`      | Six Gource MP4s of the repository history                              |
| `scripts/media-manifest.mjs`     | File hashes, dimensions, frame counts, duration and capture provenance |

Weapon GIFs use 480-pixel width, ten frames per second and up to 96 colours. Feature GIFs use
640-pixel width; the battle clip uses 640 pixels and twelve frames per second. The final jetpack
descent is shortened by advancing the real simulation, then showing its safe landing. Social
videos keep the existing 1080×1350, H.264/AAC format and scripted captions; their audio track is
silent. Game sounds remain synthesized live in Web Audio.

The scripts assert real outcomes: detonation, damage, crate pickup, guidance, rope attachment and
release, jetpack landing, flooding and shared victory. Browser errors fail a capture. The
[manifest](media-capture.json) inventories every checked-in media asset with its SHA-256 and format
facts. It records the game source fingerprint and build entry hash, avoiding an unsupported claim
that an uncommitted capture already belongs to a future Git commit.

The history chart describes committed repository history through the last gameplay commit used
for the refresh. Only a verified current coverage report is added to that commit's cache when the
core sources match HEAD. Historical measurements and archived prose keep their original dates.

   Failure scenario: Any of these produces malformed or rejected log lines, so files are missing or misplaced in the clip: a contributor or mailmap name with '|'; a type-change entry ('T', e.g. a file replaced by a symlink); or a path with non-ASCII characters, which git quotes as "docs/\303\244.md" under the default core.quotePath.    Failure scenario: Running outside a repo, in a shallow clone with a bad ref, or with a git config error makes the script stop silently before rendering. No diagnostic is printed and no MP4 is written.

   Failure scenario: Gource takes longer to start than expected, or the playback runs past 10 s. `-t $DURATION` then cuts the clip before the finished tree. The 'last second holds the finished tree' promise is never checked, so a truncated clip is still committed and recorded in the manifest.

   Failure scenario: Any change to one classifier but not the other (case folding, a new extension rule, dotfile handling) makes the legend counts disagree with the video colours. Each render also runs `git ls-files` 7 times. Fix: classify once (one awk pass over `git ls-files` with the same map) and reuse it.

6. `linkedin/render-gource.sh:59`: Two pipelines each rewrite commit timestamps to one-day steps (the awk on `--raw` output at line 31 and `coloured_log`), so two log formats and two pacing rules have to be kept in step.

   Failure scenario: A change to the pacing (for example 1700000000 + 86400*n) has to be made in two places, or the 'names' clip runs at a different pace from the other five. Simpler: generate the custom log once and use `--log-format custom` for every preset, leaving the colour field empty for the presets that don't colour files.

7. `docs/MEDIA.md:74`: `render-gource.sh` is listed as a media owner, but the 'Reproduce the entire refresh' section, its dependency list (gource, Pillow, Noto fonts) and `npm run refresh-media` do not include it.

   Failure scenario: AGENTS.md says: "Refresh affected screenshots, weapon/feature GIFs and social captions when visible rules change; update the manifest with the generated files." The Gource clips show repository history, so they go stale with every commit, yet `npm run refresh-media` never regenerates them. The manifest keeps hashing old clips, and a contributor following the documented refresh cannot reproduce them.

8. `docs/MEDIA.md:100`: MEDIA.md still says social videos 'keep the existing 1080×1350, H.264/AAC format' with a silent audio track. The new Gource social clips have no audio stream and are 1080×1080 and 1920×1080.

   Failure scenario: The docs now contradict the checked-in assets: the Gource MP4s have no audio stream (the linkedin README says 'without audio'), and three of them are not 1080×1350. Anyone checking media against MEDIA.md, or extending media-manifest checks to match it, sees the mismatch.

9. `linkedin/render-gource.sh:172`: The script needs bash 4.4+ (`mapfile`, and `"${extra[@]}"` on an empty array under `set -u`), but the shebang is `/usr/bin/env bash` and nothing checks the version.

   Failure scenario: On macOS's default bash 3.2, the non-overlay presets die with 'extra[@]: unbound variable' in `render`, and the names preset fails with 'mapfile: command not found'.

10. `docs/tasks.md:179`: The new rows T165 and T166 were inserted above T164, which breaks the table's chronological ID order.

    Failure scenario: AGENTS.md says `docs/tasks.md` should hold 'Every request with status and version'. With the rows out of order, T164 (1.83.3) appears after T166 (1.83.5), so reading down the table no longer follows the request and version history.
